lines.en: F. 35v. It must be known that the Greeks [said] the seven days of the seven planets

lines.en: administer; in which also the supposed gods of the Greeks were honored and

lines.text: Τὴν μὲν πρώτην ἔνειμαν τοῦ Ἡλίου, διὸ καὶ ἡμεῖς, ταύτην τοῦ Ἡλίου
lines.en: The first they assigned to the Sun, wherefore we too, dedicating this to the Sun

lines.en: of righteousness, Christ God 1.

lines.en: The second to the Moon; but we, as a second light, the angels in

lines.en: this day we have dedicated.

lines.text: Τὴν δὲ τρίτην τοῦ Ἄρεως· ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Προδρόμου, ὡς ἔλεγχον τῶν
lines.en: And the third to Ares; but we to the Forerunner, as a reproof of

lines.text: ἀθεμίτων πράξεων.
lines.en: lawless deeds.

lines.text: Τὴν δὲ τετάρτην τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ· ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Σταυροῦ, ὅτι ὁ μὲν Ἑρμῆς
lines.en: And the fourth to Hermes; but we to the Cross, because Hermes

lines.text: ἔφορος ὢν λόγου καὶ διδαχῆς· ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ Σταυροῦ τοῖς μὲν
lines.en: being overseer of speech and teaching; but the word of the Cross to those

lines.text: ἀπολλυμένοις μωρία ἐστίν, τοῖς δὲ σωζομένοις δύναμις Θεοῦ.
lines.en: perishing is foolishness, but to those being saved it is the power of God.

lines.text: Τὴν δὲ πέμπτην τοῦ Διός, ἡμεῖς δὲ τῶν Ἀποστόλων.
lines.en: And the fifth to Zeus, but we to the Apostles.

lines.text: Τὴν δὲ ἕκτην τῆς Ἀφροδίτης, ἡμεῖς δὲ τὴν Θεοτόκον ὀδυρομένην διὰ
lines.en: And the sixth to Aphrodite, but we to the Theotokos lamenting because of

lines.text: τὴν τοῦ υἱοῦ σταύρωσιν.
lines.en: the crucifixion of her son.

lines.text: Τὴν δὲ ἑβδόμην τοῦ Κρόνου· φασὶ γὰρ τοῦτον πατέρα θεῶν· ἡμεῖς
lines.en: And the seventh to Kronos; for they say he is the father of gods; but we

lines.text: δὲ τὸν Πατέρα ἡμῶν καὶ Θεὸν ἱκετεύομεν ὑπὲρ τῶν προαπελθόντων
lines.en: supplicate our Father and God on behalf of the departed

lines.text: πατέρων καὶ ἀδελφῶν. F. C.
lines.en: fathers and brothers. F. C.

lines.en: of Julian of Laodicea, but, as mostly happens, concerning his life we have found out almost nothing.

sections.en: 1 Very often by Christian writers the Sun of Righteousness (Malach. IV, 2) is opposed to the god Sol Invictus; cf. my Monum. myst. Mithra, I, 355; Kellner, Heortologie, 1901, p. 102. — It is pleasing to compare what the anonymous author edited in Catal. Mediol., p. 32 ss. has collected concerning the days of the Moon.

summary.headline: Julian’s Christian Planetary Week
summary.text: Julian of Laodicea’s astronomical disquisition assigns the seven planetary days to the Sun, Moon, Ares, Hermes, Zeus, Aphrodite, and Kronos, then gives them Christian meanings involving Christ, angels, the Forerunner, the Cross, the Apostles, the Theotokos, and prayers for the departed. An editorial note introduces Julian, whose life and date remain uncertain.
